items.title: Pay 'Aktualisierungsgebühr' (vehicle data update fee)
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed calendar date for payment: 'zahlbar bis 30.11.2026'. 2026-11-30 is a Monday, not a weekend or public holiday in NW, so no shift applies. This is taken as written from a private sender, not a statutory deadline computed under BGB rules.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of a known scam pattern (similar to fake 'Gewerbeauskunft' or fake vehicle-register extortion letters): an official-sounding name ('Zentralregister Fahrzeugdaten Deutschland') paired with only a PO box, demanding an unsolicited fee and threatening consequences ('kann die Zulassung ab Januar 2027 ruhen', 'melden wir den Vorgang der zuständigen Zulassungsstelle') to create pressure.

The payment IBAN is foreign (Lithuania, LT) and the named recipient 'R. Kazlauskas' is an individual person, not the sending organisation — a German vehicle register would not collect fees to a personal foreign account; do not pay without independently verifying this organisation exists and is legitimate (e.g. via the real KBA/Zulassungsstelle, not via contact details on this letter).

There is no German state body called 'Zentralregister Fahrzeugdaten Deutschland' responsible for vehicle registration fees; genuine Halterdaten changes are handled free or for a small official fee directly by the local Zulassungsstelle, never by private postal-box services demanding bank transfers to foreign personal accounts.
The letter contains no legal-remedy instructions (Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung), consistent with it not being an official administrative decision despite its authority-like tone.
